name: Bayer

summary.text: Bayer is a German pharmaceutical and crop science company. It acquired the U.S. seed and agrochemical company Monsanto in 2018 for $63 billion, making crop protection its largest business and bringing with it litigation over the glyphosate herbicide Roundup. After three jury-trial losses, Bayer announced in June 2020 that it would pay up to $10.9 billion to resolve most of the Roundup litigation, without admitting wrongdoing and while continuing to sell the product. ETC Group's surveys of patents on so-called climate-ready crop genes list Bayer among the companies holding most such patent families.

facts.claim: Bayer acquired Monsanto in 2018 for $63 billion, a deal that made crop protection Bayer's largest business, ahead of pharmaceuticals, and brought with it thousands of lawsuits over the Roundup herbicide.
facts.quote: the company acquired in its $63-billion acquisition of the agrochemical and seed company, Monsanto, in 2018.

sources.title: Bayer inks largest settlement in pharma history with $10B Roundup deal
How Monsanto's Roundup Herbicide Went From Bayer Asset to Burden

facts.claim: In June 2020 Bayer announced a settlement of between $10.1 billion and $10.9 billion to resolve Roundup litigation: $8.8 billion to $9.6 billion for current claims, which Bayer said covered about 75% of roughly 125,000 filed and unfiled claims, plus up to $1.25 billion for a separate class agreement addressing potential future claims.
facts.quote: Bayer said the settlement would bring closure to approximately 75% of the current Roundup litigation involving approximately 125,000 filed and unfiled claims overall.

facts.claim: In announcing the 2020 Roundup settlement Bayer stated that it did not change the company's view that glyphosate is safe and does not cause cancer, and that it would continue to sell Roundup; the settlement contained no admission of wrongdoing.
facts.quote: The deal does not change Bayer's view that glyphosate, the active ingredient in Roundup, is safe and does not cause cancer.

facts.claim: Bloomberg Law reported that three jury-trial losses over Roundup after the Monsanto acquisition drove down Bayer's share price and prompted a shareholder revolt against management.
facts.quote: Three jury-trial losses tanked shares and sparked a revolt among shareholders angry at Bayer's management

sources.title: How Monsanto's Roundup Herbicide Went From Bayer Asset to Burden

facts.claim: ETC Group's October 2010 report on patents claiming environmental stress tolerance in plants found that DuPont, Monsanto, BASF, Bayer, Syngenta and their partners accounted for 77% of 262 patent families identified between June 2008 and June 2010; an earlier ETC survey counted Bayer as holding 5 of 55 such families. ETC Group is an advocacy organisation and the counts were not independently verified.
facts.quote: DuPont, Monsanto, BASF, Bayer, Syngenta and their biotech partners account for three-quarters (77%) of the patent families identified.
